posts.raw_content:
This is just a long rambling thinking-out-loud thing.  If that will bother you, don't even complain.  Just skip it.  "You're welcome" for this warning.

First, a digression:

Decades ago,  I walked into a Temp Agency-- took a typing test-- and the next day they sent me to a hospital.  Where I was given an office & a secretary & a fax machine.  I had NO medical training.

Each morning, the doctors would tell me how many beds had opened-up in the specialize Neurology ward & the Orthopedic ward.   That's broken brains & broken bones.   Usually zero, one... maybe two or three beds.

Other hospitals would fax their patient's medical charts to me.  I was supposed to read them & pick who we would admit.    At first, the doctors got mad at me, "Why are you sending us all these SICK PEOPLE?!!"

One guy was 400 lbs.   He needed a special bed, was hard to roll him over to change his sheets.  And I didn't know the word "Decubitus" meant he had oozing bed sores, just from lying in bed constantly.     Other patients had the flu, which could spread to our patients.  Other hospitals were eager to dump them on us.

The hospital management was playing cost cutting games by hiring me.  Union staff were negotiating a contract/ threatening to strike.    The hospital management could hire an endless series of cheap temps like me-- as long as they cut us within 90 days.  Rather than fill the position with an actual salary/benefits career person.   

The reason I started with that story-- is because it was an example of me stumbling effortlessly into a situation where I had 'no business' being.  Which has happened to me many times over the years.

And I'm in a situation like that now.  But I don't want to dox the specific details.   So I told that other story, instead.

Now I have a front row seat to watching an old man lose his mind & his health.  And soon he will die.   

The strange part is-- we just met.  We aren't related.  Nor have we become friends.  He doesn't even like me-- except for occasionally realizing he needs my help. Which results in a coin-toss... whether he'll feel a moment of gratitude or a moment of resentment.  Before his attention shifts away from me again. In fairness-- I don't like him much either.  It's work-related, but I'm not dependent on him for my job & paycheck.   Yet I have access to his private correspondence, his bank records, his medical charts, the private thoughts he blurts-out/ then forgets he told me.

It just occurred to me-- that this situation might be commonplace.  I'm imagining some young newlywed suddenly realizing the marriage includes taking care of your spouse's dying relative.  Unrewarding intimate access to a strange stranger, with burdens of responsibility.    But that would entail a family bond-- by marriage not blood, but still...

I'm not going inherit anything from this old fart.  I owe him nothing beyond common courtesy.   And he has a stingy view of doling-out common courtesy--  which makes me feel even-less obligated.

I started typing this because the Joe Biden comparison popped-into my head.   Imagine being some random immigrant Teleprompter repairman or Hair Plug masseuse... or his AIPAC Handler (Biden's record stands as the all-time-career #1 AIPAC donation-recipient in Congress.)    In other words: imagine someone who feels no particular patriotic duty while watching Biden drool ice-cream & say weird shit in speakerphone calls with Hunter's business associates.   10% brain function for the Big Guy.

Heck-- it's kinda-like if you were one of the random 60 guys on that Cornell frat groupchat.    You didn't even attend that party.  You went to bed early.  You woke up to a wall of texts about some slut happily blowing every guy in sight.   2 years later-- people are mad at you for not calling 911 & not slut-shaming a polyamorous girl boss.   Too Much Information... not-enough reason to consider that a "me" problem.

This old guy I'm dealing with--  I don't know if he technically has Alzheimers.  Or if he's just having an endless series of mentally-muddled Bad Days due-to decrepitude & poor sleep.     

Does that distinction even matter?   Like all the rest of this-- it's not really my problem to care-about or deal-with.    Yet I have a bizarre frontrow view of it all.   Which is why it's on my mind in the middle of the night.

posts.raw_content: I have my ticket. I’m really just wondering if I should be there way early. I hear it can be fun. I’m also wondering if there is anything that may not be obvious that I can’t bring in. I’m going to be walking to the event. I am currently experiencing some vehicle issues but I’m trying to achieve 15,500 steps a day anyway. That’s minimum and I’m a little behind because I got a shin splint from pushing my truck out of an intersection when it quit on me. That seems to be fine now after a few days of taking it easier. I figured I’d walk and save the parking for others and catch up on the steps and calories I’m attempting to burn. I’d like to bring a water bottle. Maybe a pen light since it will be dark when I walk home after the event. I don’t really need the water bottle. I can use something disposable. I won’t have a vehicle in which to place anything prohibited. I plan to travel light. Just those items, my wallet, my phone, and a disposable poncho because there is a chance of rain. I was wondering about that item. I can stash that somewhere on my walk to fetch on my walk home. If they open that thing to observe it, I’ll never get it folded back. I was also wondering if they have water for purchase at the events for my walk back. My BP meds are a diuretic. I can get dried out. I haven’t looked to see what stores my be on my route. I’m sure there is something. I’m excited. Just prepping some food for the slow cooker so dinner is hot and ready when I get home. He wanted to attend a rally for at least a decade. 🎉
